verification.note:
addons/intelligence/frontend/SceneCandidatesSection.tsx:48 computes `isLoft = segment.filename.toLowerCase().endsWith(".loft")` and :62-72 renders a blank `
` instead of `` when isLoft. SceneCandidatesSection.test.tsx:208-229 asserts no for ref.loft / ref.LOFT and one for the mp4. The touch-point list names no frontend file. docs/specs/youtube-frames.md:365-367 says 'A frontend change ... no UI change is planned; R-5 confirms', and :154 says 'the UI never requests a .loft frame, so no new UI'. Before this change a .loft had no clip rows and so could not appear as a scene candidate, which is consistent with the guard being new in this change. I could not run git diff, so I did not see directly that the file is in the diff. decisions.md:7 (second R-5 run) records two blank cards for nn-youtube.loft and no /frame request.

docs/user-guide/search.md:115 says 'Its picture is read from YouTube when the candidates load, so it can appear a few seconds after the others and stays blank when YouTube cannot be read.' The code at addons/intelligence/frontend/SceneCandidatesSection.tsx:62 always renders the blank div for a .loft filename and never calls getFrameUrl for it, so the picture is never read and the card is always blank. docs/addons/intelligence.md:212 describes the code correctly ('shows a blank card rather than asking the frame route for its picture'), so the two documents contradict each other.

addons/intelligence/app/youtube_source.py:39-55 defines `_SIGNED_FETCH` (ytimg.com|googlevideo.com|youtube.com|sigh=|sqp=) and `_SignedFetchFilter`. At module import, `_drop_signed_fetches()` adds that filter once to `logging.getLogger("httpx")`. The module is imported at module level by workers/clip.py:30, routers/scenes.py:21 and rag/file_question.py:30, and lazily by routers/files.py:1573, so the filter applies to the whole process from startup. The filter drops only records whose message matches those patterns, so other httpx callers (for example http://backend:8000, which decisions.md:7/13/19 shows still logged) are unaffected. It is still a process-wide logging change outside the listed touch points. The comment at youtube_source.py:35-38 gives the reason for the choice.

specification_compliance: The frontend guard (SceneCandidatesSection.tsx:48,62) contradicts the spec's statement that no UI change is planned (youtube-frames.md:365-367). It does match the spec's failure-table claim that the UI never requests a .loft frame (youtube-frames.md:154).
docs/user-guide/search.md:115 contradicts both the code and docs/addons/intelligence.md:212 about whether a YouTube candidate's picture is fetched.
I5 (no log line contains a URL): the httpx logger filter at youtube_source.py:39-55 is how the code enforces it for the sheet downloads made with httpx.get (clip.py:1062).
potential_unspecified_behavior: Any httpx log record in the process whose message contains youtube.com, ytimg.com, googlevideo.com, sigh= or sqp= is now dropped, whichever caller produced it.
Scene candidate cards for any file whose name ends in .loft, case-insensitively, are always blank, including YouTube references whose frame route works.
regression_risks: Users who read the user guide expect YouTube candidate pictures to load after a delay; they never do.
A future httpx caller whose URLs contain youtube.com would lose its request logs with no visible cause.
test_coverage: SceneCandidatesSection.test.tsx:208-229 covers the .loft blank card for lower and upper case and the native video's .
I did not find a test asserting the httpx filter's scope (that non-YouTube httpx records still pass).
not_verified: Whether SceneCandidatesSection.tsx and its test are actually in the diff against origin/develop: git diff could not be run, and the claim that the code is new rests on reasoning and decisions.md.
Whether the httpx library logs to the 'httpx' logger itself rather than a child logger in the pinned version, which decides whether the filter takes effect.
The rest of the change's invariants (I1-I10) beyond these three findings.
